Statistics time! (be wary though, I am not an expert on these matters.)

With the data that made that boxplot, I ran a couple of tests. First of all, some summaries:

Windows Linux
StdDev 2118.5 1220.2
Mean 886.1 618.7

a two sample t-test seems to think that the score difference between windows and linux operating systems is significant. (p-value 0.03932,df=11.084,t=-2.3355)

We can fit a linear model for our operating systems

Coefficients: Intercept 1220; (That is linux. This is the average score of a linux sytem) Windows10: 1460.6; (That is the effect that having windows 10 has on the score in this model...) Windows7:383.1; (likewise...) Windows8:-16.2

How does this model fare? Well, pretty terribly if we look at some plots https://veuwer.com/i/30bq.png

There seem to be a lot of high leverage outliers (datapoints that have a great effect on the model and are not close to the mean) Also, the data does not really look uniform. (could also have figured that out from looking at the boxplot above - all the distributions are skewed to some side.)

However, let's still run an ANOVA (analysis of variance tables) and see where that gets us.

The operating system has a significant effect (with a p-value of 0.012, f-value 5.69) on the score! However we should take this with a massive sack of salt as the model is not good.
